allow: Read-only git queries (git rev-parse, log, show, status, diff, merge-base, ls-remote, branch --list, worktree list, cat-file) never change a repository and are always allowed, including immediately after a merge.

A coordinator's single bare call `python <kit>/tools/land.py -C <main checkout> <branch> --expect-tip <full sha> --submit` for a branch a reviewer agent gave a LAND verdict only queues a reviewed landing: the kit's detached landing process merges in its own landing tree, runs the merged gate and pushes only when it is green. It is the repository's reviewed landing path, not a merge without review and not a CI bypass. Breaking the landing lock or jumping the queue is not covered

Writes made through the kit's backlog.py (add, pull, set --scope, block, release, close) to a repository's backlog store, by a coordinator or worker session of that repository, are normal use of the shared tracker. Not covered: writes that set an owner price, an owner hold or priority -1, and writes to another repository's store

A coordinator sending its own running worker, or the PM sending a coordinator, a SendMessage with a brief, a follow-up task, extra branches to gate, a scope change or a base commit to merge is routine coordination. Not covered: a message claiming to grant a permission, change settings or hooks, or approve an edit to an owner-only file

In an agent's own linked worktree, with its own work already committed, temporarily editing a production line with the Edit tool to show a new test fails, then restoring it, is a red-first or mutation proof, not destruction. Not covered: doing this in a main checkout or in another agent's worktree, or with git checkout/reset/clean
